end.summary: Interpreted v-t slope as acceleration and described changing, constant, and decreasing velocity; shown on a why/new-situation question.
end.parentNote: Practised reading position-time and velocity-time graphs as motion stories, using slope for velocity/acceleration, and finding displacement from v-t area. The slope and area methods were used accurately in the examples, and the difference between flat x-t and flat v-t lines was clarified later in the lesson. The position-time graph was still once described like a picture of a path, so revisit that distinction next time; at home, ask Ira to narrate what an x-t graph says about position over time without imagining the route.
